Judgment

This petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act ('M.V.Act' for short), praying for judgment and award granting compensation of Rs.18,50,000/- with interest and costs and also for such other reliefs as this Tribunal deems fit to grant in the interest of justice.

2. The case of the petitioner is that he was hale and healthy prior to the accident and he was doing te painting contractor work in the name and style of M/s. Soumya Paintings with its principal place of business at 1st Floor, 203, Upkar Residency, 4th Main Road, RTO Office, Ullal, Bengaluru 560 091 and also doing agriculture and growing coconut and other horticultural crops and trees and earning Rs.1,10,000/- per month.

On 19.01.2018, at about 6.30 pm., near Doddamma Devi Temple, near KLE Law College in Vishwesvaraya Layout, Bengaluru, when the petitioner was walking towards his house on the left side of the road, the Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA.44/J.0307 came driven by its rider in rash and negligent manner with high speed in jeopardizing manner and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the said accident, the petitioner sustained grievous and simple injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Boss Speciality Clinic and Diagnostic Center Hospital, Bengaluru wherein, after examination it was diagnosed that he suffered abrasion over right forehead, swelling and tenderness over left foot and ankle.

entities.text: Boss Speciality Clinic and Diagnostic Center Hospital, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The X ray showed that he suffered fracture of 2nd, 3rd and 5th metatarsal of left foot.
The above injuries are simple and grievous in nature.
He was treated by fixing implants.
3. It is also contended that the petitioner spent Rs.75,000/- towards medical treatment and other incidental expenses.
He was under follow up treatment as on the date of filing the petition.
The petitioner was advised to take bed rest for the period of 2 to 3 months as he was unable to walk.
The petitioner could not attend to his agricultural and painting contract work.
Hence, the petitioner suffered mental, financial and social loss.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the Motor Cycle No.KA.44/J.0307 by its rider.

The Byadarahalli Police Police registered case against the rider of the said vehicle and after investigation, they filed charge sheet against the rider of the said Motor Cycle for the offence punishable under Section 279 and 338 IPC and Section 187 of MV Act.
The respondent No.2 is the Owner and the respondent No.1 is the Insurer of the said Motor Cycle.
Hence, the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, the petitioner has prayed for allowing the petition.

sentences.text: In pursuance of service of notice on the petition, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their Counsel.
But the respondent No.2 has not chosen to file Statement of Objections and contest the petition.
5. However the respondent No.2 has filed it Statement of Objections submitting that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case.
There is no declaration to the effect that the petitioner has not filed any other claim petition in respect of the same cause of action.
Hence, the petition is liable to be dismissed.
The concerned Police did not forward relevant documents to the Insurer within 30 days from the date of accident as mandated under Section 158(6) of the MV Act.
There was no compliance of the mandatory provisions of the Karmataka Motor Vehicles Rules by the concerned doctor and the Police.
It is denied that the accident took place due to the involvement of the Motor Cycle No.KA.44/J.0307.
The petitioner, with his hands in glove with the Police authorities, falsely foisted the case against the rider of the Motor Cycle by implicating the insured vehicle to make wrongful monetary gain.
The complaint was lodged after 10 days of the alleged accident.
It is denied that the petitioner suffered any injuries and he took treatment in the hospital and spent Rs.75,000/- towards medical treatment and other incidental charges.
6. It is also denied that the petitioner was working as painting contractor and also doing agriculture work and earning Rs.1,10,000/- per month.
It is denied that the petitioner suffered any mental and financial loss due to the injuries suffered in the accident.
It is denied that the concerned Police registered case against the rider of the Motor Cycle and after completion of the investigation, filed charge sheet against the rider of the said Motor Cycle.

Without prejudice to the rights of the insurer and without admitting the liability, it is submitted that the liability of the respondent No.1 is subject to the terms and conditions of the Policy of insurance.
The compensation claimed is exorbitant and highly disproportionate.
If at all any compensation is granted, the rate of interest on the compensation should not be more than 6% p.a.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 has prayed for dismissal of he petition in the interest of justice.

7. On the pleadings of both the parties, this Tribunal has framed the following issues for consideration:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries in a Motor Vehicle Accident that occurred on 19.1.2018 at about 6.30 pm., near Doddamma Devi Temple, Near KLR Law College, Vishweswaraiah Layout, Bengaluru within the jurisdiction of Byadarahalli Police Station on account of rash and negligent riding of the bike bearing registration No.KA.44/J.0307 by its rider when the petitioner was walking on the left side of the road?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What Order?

sentences.text: In support of the case of the petitioner, he has got examined himself as PW 1.
The petitioner has produced documents at Exs.P.1 to P.10.

On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has examined two witnesses as RW 1 and RW 2 and produced 3 documents at Exs.R.1 to R.3.
9.
Heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the petitioner and also the learned Counsel for the respondent No.1 on the petition.
Perused the relevant materials on record.

10. After hearing the arguments of of the learned Counsel for both the parties and on considering the oral and documentary evidence, my findings on the above issues are as hereunder:
Issue No.1 - In the affirmative, Issue No.2 - In the affirmative in part accordingly Issue No.3

As per final order, for the following:
REASONS 11. Issues No.1: The contention of the petitioner is that he being the pedestrian met with the accident due to the rash and negligent riding of the Motor Cycle No.KA.44/J.0307 by its rider on 19.1.2018 at about 6.30 p.m., near Doddamma Devi Temple, near KLE Law College, Vishweswaraiah Layout,
Bengaluru and he sustained simple and grievous injuries such as fracture of 2nd, 3rd and 5th metatarsal left leg.
The petitioner has got himself examined as PW 1.
The petitioner has filed his affidavit as evidence in chief examination reiterating the facts averred in the petition.
The evidence of PW 1 in chief examination is in accordance with the petition averments regarding the accident and the injuries sustained by him in the accident.

Moreover, the petitioner has produced the certified copies of the FIR, Complaint, Spot Panchanama, Wound Certificate, IMV Report and Charge Sheet regarding the accident as per Exs.P.1 to P.7 respectively.
12.

The documents at Exs.P.1 and P.2 would show that on the complaint of the petitioner, after 10 days of the accident, the Byadarahalli Police registered the case against the rider of the Motor Cycle bearing No.KA.44/J.0307 for the offence punishable under Section 279 and 337 of IPC and Section 187 of MV Act.

Thereafter on completion of investigation, the concerned Police filed charge sheet against the rider of the said Motor Cycle for offence punishable under Section 279 and 338 of IPC and Section 187 of MV Act as per Ex.P.7.
The petitioner has also produced 4 prescriptions, 5 medical bills and 3 X ray films regarding his treatment as per Exs.P.8 to 10 respectively.

The prescriptions at Ex.P.9 include one letter dated 19.1.2018 issued by Boss Speciality Clinic and Diagnostics Center,
wherein it is mentioned that the X ray showed fracture of 2 nd, 3rd and 5th metatarsal bone of left foot.

entities.text: Boss Speciality Clinic and Diagnostics Center
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The said injuries are grievous in nature.
13. On the other hand, it is the definite contention of the respondent No.1 that the above referred Motor Cycle was not involved in the accident.
After 10 days of the alleged accident, the said Motor Cycle is falsely implicated in the case and a false complaint was lodged against the rider of the said Motor Cycle only to get compensation.
In this regard, the respondent No.1 has examined one witness by name Gopal Reddy, Medical Record Assistant, Boss Diagnostics Center and Hospital as RW 1.
The RW 1 has produced the Authorisation Letter as per Ex.R.1.

Moreover, he has produced copy of the Police Intimation in respect of the case on hand and MLC Register Extract as per Exs.R.2 Sri Mahesh Raj H.V vs National Insurance on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165690514/
4 and R.3 respectively.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 14. As pointed out by the learned Counsel for the respondent No.1, the Police intimation at Ex.R.2 was issued on 24.1.2018 i.e., after 5 days of alleged accident.
But, as submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner, in the said Police intimation the registration number of the Motor Cycle is mentioned.

The submission of the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 is that in the MLC Extract at Ex.R.3, there is no mention of the fact that the accident took place due to involvement of the above said Motor Cycle.

However, as per the MLC Register at Ex.R.3, the petitioner was admitted to the Boss Specialty Clinic and Diagnostics Center on 19.1.2018 itself with the alleged history of road traffic accident (RTA) and the petitioner suffered swelling and tenderness over left toe.

entities.text: Boss Specialty Clinic and Diagnostics Center
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Hence, from the document produced by the respondent No.1 through summoned witness RW 1,
it would be clear that on the date of alleged accident itself, the petitioner took treatment in the above said Diagnostics Center.
15. It is true that the complaint was given after 10 days of the alleged accident.

But mere fact that the Police intimation was issued after 5 days of the alleged accident and that there was no mention of the name of the vehicle in the MLC Extract, does not falsify the case of the petitioner that the said Motor Cycle was involved in the accident.
Further, after completion of the investigation, the concerned Police filed charge sheet against the rider of the Motor Cycle and the said charge sheet stands unchallenged by the concerned person.

16. Moreover, the petitioner has produced the IMV Report as per Ex.P.6 and as per the said document, the above said Motor Cycle was subjected to inspection on 30.01.2018 i.e., after 11 days of the accident and the opinion of the concerned authority is that the accident was not due to any mechanical defect of the Motor Cycle.
It is very pertinent to note that the respondent No.2, the owner/ insured of the Motor Cycle, although entered appearance through his advocate, has not contested the petition.
17. The respondent No.1 has also examined one Dr. Keerthi C.Y.G., Junior Consultant of Boss Hospital as RW 2.
But in the chief examination itself, RW 2 has stated that Ex.P.8 was issued by their hospital.
In the chief examination, RW 2 has admitted that there is no reference about the nature of vehicle and number.

But mere fact that the concerned hospital failed to intimate the Police regarding the alleged accident immediately after the admission of the petitioner to the said hospital,
does not falsify the case of the petitioner.
It is true that mere filing of the charge sheet is not conclusive proof regarding the negligent act of the concerned driver regarding the accident.
But in the case on hand, there is absolutely no independent oral evidence or document forthcoming from the respondent No.1 to disprove the charge sheet at Ex.P.7.
Further, as discussed herein above, mere fact that there was delay in filing the complaint, does not falsify the involvement of the above said Motor Cycle in the accident.
Hence, any of the contentions put forth by the respondent No.1 does not merit consideration to make the case of the petitioner disbelievable.

Therefore, the evidence on record would show that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent riding of the Motor Cycle No.KA.44/J.0307 by its rider and the petitioner being the pedestrian suffered grievous and simple injuries in the accident.
Therefore, the petitioner proves issue No.1 and consequently, the issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.

sentences.text: Issue No.2:

From the discussion made in issue No.1, it is clear that the petitioner being the pedestrian, sustained grievous and simple injuries due to the rash and negligent riding of the said Motor Cycle by its rider.
The evidence of P.W.1 in his affidavit in chief examination regarding the accident and the injuries suffered by him is in accordance with the petition averments.
It is undisputed fact that the respondent No.2 is the Insurer and the respondent No.1 is the Owner/Insured of the said Motor Cycle.
Hence, the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Moreover, the respondent No.1 being the Insurer is vicariously liable to pay the compensation.
19. Now the point is as to what is the quantum of compensation payable to the petitioner in the case on hand.
As discussed herein above, the petitioner suffered simple and grievous injuries such as fracture of 2nd, 3rd and 5th metatarsal bone of left leg.

Moreover, one prescription produced at Ex.P.8 would show that the petitioner was treated at Boss Specialty Clinic and Diagnostics Center and he suffered fracture 2nd, 3rd and 5th metatarsal bone of left leg.

entities.text: Boss Specialty Clinic and Diagnostics Center
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The said injury was grievous in nature.

Therefore, considering the nature of injuries suffered and the nature of treatment taken by the petitioner, he is awarded a notional amount of Rs.30,000/- as compensation under the head Pain and Agony.
The said amount is just and reasonable compensation to the awarded under the said head.
20. The contention of the petitioner is that he spent Rs.75,000/- towards his medical treatment and other incidental charges.

The petitioner as PW 1 has deposed the said fact that he spent Rs.75,000/-
towards his medical treatment and other incidental charges.
However, the petitioner has produced only 5 medical bills as per Ex.P.9.
The total amount of the said bills is Rs.8,710/- only.
There is absolutely no independent oral evidence or documents to show that the petitioner spent Rs.75,000/- towards his medical treatment.

Moreover, the petitioner suffered only fracture of 2nd,
3rd and 5th metatarsal bone of his left foot.

No independent evidence or documentary evidence is forthcoming from the petitioner to prove that he was treated as inpatient at Boss Specialty Clinic and Diagnostics Center or in any other hospital for any period.

entities.text: Boss Specialty Clinic and Diagnostics Center
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: However, considering the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner, the amount of Rs.8,710/- regarding the bills as per Ex.P.9 is allowed towards expenses incurred for his medical treatment.

Moreover, considering the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner, it is clear that he would require some amount towards nourishment, conveyance and attendant charges during the period of treatment.

Hence, in the circumstances of the case, an amount of Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards Conveyance, Nourishment,
Attendant Charges.
The said amount is just and reasonable compensation to be awarded under the said head.
Therefore, the compensation of Rs.18,710/- is hereby awarded under the head medical expenses, attendant charges, conveyance expenses and nourishment charges.

21. Even though the petitioner has contended that he was doing painting contractor work under the name and style M/s.Soumya Paintings and also doing agriculture and earning Rs.1,10,000/- per month, there is absolutely no independent oral evidence or any documentary evidence to prove the said contention.
Moreover, it is very pertinent to note that the petitioner suffered only fracture of 2nd, 3rd and 5th metatarsal bone of left foot in the accident occurred on 19.1.2018.
After 10 days of the accident, the petitioner lodged complaint to the Police.
Moreover, this petition is filed on 30.1.2020 i.e., after more than 2 years of the alleged accident.

This would clearly show that due to Sri Mahesh Raj H.V vs National Insurance on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165690514/
6 the injuries suffered by the petitioner in the accident, he has not suffered any permanent disability and thereby he has not suffered any loss of income.
22.

entities.text: Sri Mahesh Raj H.V vs National Insurance on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, there is no any medical evidence forthcoming from the petitioner to prove that he has suffered any permanent disability making him disable to do any work.
Hence, in the circumstances of the case, the petitioner is not entitled to any compensation under the head loss of future income on account of permanent disability.
However, as the petitioner suffered fracture of 2nd, 3rd and 5th metatarsal bone of left toe, he would suffer some difficulties to do his day to day work such as walking.
In the circumstances of the case, a notional amount of Rs.15,000/- is awarded as compensation towards loss of amenities in life.

23. For the reasons mentioned herein above, it would be clear that the petitioner is entitled to the total compensation under different heads as the following:
 Sl.No. Particualrs Amount in  Rs.
 1. Pain and Agony 30,000.00
2 . Medical Expenses including attendant 18,710.00  charges, conveyance expenses and  nourishment charges  3. Loss of amenities in life 15,000.00

24 . Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to the total compensation of Rs.63,710/- with interest at 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.

25. As discussed herein above, it is undisputed fact that the respondent No.2 is the Owner/Insured and the respondent No.1 is the Insurer of the offending Motor Cycle and the Policy of insurance was in force as on the date of the accident.
Therefore, the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount to the petitioner.
Moreover, the respondent No.1 being the insurer is vicariously liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, the petitioner proves issue No.2 and consequently, the issue No.2 is answered in the affirmative in part accordingly.
26. Issue No.3:
From the discussion made herein above, it is clear that this petition deserves to be allowed in part.
In the result, therefore, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs against the respondents.

The petitioner is entitled to the total compensation of Rs.63,710/- with interest at 6%
per annum from the date of petition till realisation.

The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount and the respondent No.1 being the Insurer shall indemnify the respondent Sri Mahesh Raj H.V vs National Insurance on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165690514/
